invalid.claim: B has been preparing for the visa application

decisions.reason: A's definite possessive 'your visa application' in turn 1 directly attributes the application to B.

decisions.claim: B wants a visa to America
decisions.reason: A's question 'why do you want a visa to America?' presupposes B wants a visa to America; the 'why' question form presupposes the desire exists.

decisions.claim: B plans to go to America
decisions.reason: Turn 5 is a yes/no question 'Do you plan to go to America…' which asks whether the plan exists rather than presupposing it. No definite possessive or 'why'-type presupposition is present.
decisions.counterexample: B could answer 'No, I don't plan to go to America' without contradiction.

decisions.claim: B has some preparation (for the visa application)
decisions.reason: A's 'all your preparation' in turn 7 uses a definite possessive presupposing B has preparation; the question asks about completion, not existence.
'or with your family' in a yes/no question offers an alternative; it does not presuppose B has a family. B could answer 'by myself' or 'I don't have a family' without contradiction.
decisions.counterexample: B could say 'I don't have a family, I'm going alone.'
